transit.name: Mountain Valley Transit
transit.detail: Free door-to-door rides, booked by phone, Tuesday to Friday 8 am to 4 pm. Local service is suspended from November 16, 2026 through the end of the year.

timeline.text: The Chaffee County Courthouse on East Main Street dates to 1882.
The county seat shifted to Salida, leaving the courthouse without its purpose.
By 1936 the old courthouse had become a schoolhouse, a role it kept until 1972.
Buena Vista Heritage was founded and the courthouse was saved from demolition.
After a fire, the Denver, South Park & Pacific depot was given a new use as a museum.

trails.name: Buena Vista River Park and the river trails
trails.length: The nearly flat Arkansas River Trail, 0.6 mile, makes a river loop with the Whitewater and Rock ’n Roll trails
trails.address: 800 East Main Street, at the end of East Main by the Arkansas River
trails.season: Dawn to 10 pm, the Town’s parks page says; its 2023 park rules say dawn to dusk.
trails.dogs: On a leash no longer than 20 feet; the off-leash dog park, with small- and large-dog areas, is across from the Community Center.
trails.fee: Renting the large pavilion costs $60 for under four hours.

trails.name: Hecla Junction and the Seidel’s Suckhole trail
trails.manager: Colorado Parks and Wildlife, Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area
trails.length: A ¾-mile foot trail downstream along the shore to Seidel’s Suckhole, CPW says; the BLM gives 2 miles out and back
trails.trailhead: Hecla Junction Recreation Site, the main take-out for the Browns Canyon run; the road in is steep and unpaved
trails.season: Open 24 hours a day, all year.
trails.fee: A CPW daily pass from the self-serve kiosk: $10–$12 a vehicle with Colorado plates, $15–$17 from out of state, or $4 a person; or a CPW annual pass.

trails.name: Cottonwood Lake Picnic Area
trails.manager: U.S. Forest Service, Salida Ranger District
trails.size: 17 picnic sites with tables and grills, parking for 20 vehicles, and accessible fishing docks on the shore
trails.trailhead: Follow Main Street west out of town onto County Road 306 for 6 miles, then County Road 344 for 3 miles to the lake
trails.season: Open all year, sunrise to sunset; day use only, no camping. No drinking water.
trails.dogs: On a leash at all times.
trails.fee: $10 to use the site from May to September, unless you are camping in a Salida Ranger District developed campground.
